title: Generic Rust graph core and Graph IR structural validation
objective: Implement one generic Rust graph crate with private third-party internals, deterministic algorithms, stable Grafting-owned contracts, and reuse it for Graph IR structural validation without duplicating graph semantics in JavaScript.
validations: cargo fmt check passed for grafting-graph-core
cargo clippy passed for all grafting-graph-core targets and features with warnings denied
six grafting-graph-core tests passed with all features, including public API and Graph IR CLI contracts
all six graph-core Nx targets passed: format, check, lint, test, api-check, and graph-ir-check
Graph IR v1 shape/adapter suite passed with five Node tests and the Rust structural suite
Nx recognized graph-core as a real project and the generated project graph was refreshed
Graph IR candidate generation and freshness check passed with 28 nodes and 21 edges
petgraph 0.8.3, serde 1.0.229, and serde_json 1.0.151 licenses verified as MIT OR Apache-2.0
vendor-boundary scan found @antv/x6 only in x6-canvas and petgraph only inside graph-core
coordination validation and control-plane audit passed with zero model calls and zero side effects
risks: A graph API shaped only around Graph IR would not remain reusable for other products.
Exposing petgraph or serde types would couple consumers to replaceable dependencies.
Keeping endpoint and identity validation in JavaScript would duplicate the Rust authority established by DEC-051.
Removing graph-x6 before its current application consumer is migrated would break the working spike.
The generated cross-language public API baseline remains assigned to I-003; GRAPH-001 provides a compile-time Rust API contract and behavioral tests.
The Wasm client and atomic graph-x6 removal remain future consumer-driven work; no duplicate TypeScript graph engine was introduced.
